messages:
sophia: Heads up — nightly bisect shows a tail-latency regression on the GQA/MQA paged-kv path. Observed ~+12% 99.9p for seqlen > 256. Dumping perf traces now.

liam: Is this after the kernel-selector change (PR #4123) that adjusted seqlen thresholds?

sophia: Yes — canary includes that PR. The selector picks 'paged-blockv2' more aggressively at the 256 boundary. Suspect interaction with KV fragmentation.

amar: Can you paste a quick perf summary and which workload (chat vs completion)?

sophia: Perf snippet from canary vs baseline (same host type, same traffic trace):
```
workload: chat-streaming (multiturn)
baseline (stable): 99.9p = 82ms, 95p = 30ms, avg = 18ms
canary (PR4123):   99.9p = 92ms (+12%), 95p = 31ms (+3%), avg = 18.5ms
kv_page_frag: baseline=0.62 -> canary=0.81
kernel picks: baseline prefers paged-v1 for seqlen 256-320, canary flips to paged-v2
```

jen: kv_page_frag jump +0.19 is concerning. If the new kernel has different prefetch density it could worsen warmup latency. Any flamegraph?

benchbot: Quick bench summary (automated): baseline 99.9=82ms, canary 99.9=92ms, throughput (reqs/sec) within noise (±2%).

liam: Hypothesis: seqlen gating boundary caused a kernel pick that is less tolerant to fragmented KV layout (more misses -> higher tail). Two short-term mitigations: 1) add hysteresis on seqlen gates (delay switch for N tokens) 2) score in kv_frag and prefer paged-v1 when frag>0.7.

amar: Agreed. Also want a microbench sweep: vary block_size=[32,64,128], compare paged-v1 vs paged-v2 under --kv-layout=fragmented. I can run that tomorrow.

sophia: Starting a targeted sweep now. Command I'm running: `./bench --model gqa-7b --profile --seqlen 512 --kv-layout fragmented --kernel-hint seqlen_gated --sweep block_size:32,64,128`

jen: Low-risk ops plan: roll back PR4123 on canaries that show >+8% 99.9p OR force fallback to paged-v1 when kv_frag>0.7 until we have an autotune fix. Which do we prefer?

liam: Prefer soft-fallback combined with an autotune patch: add a kv_frag score to kernel scoring and a small hysteresis window (8 tokens) to avoid flip-flopping mid-request. That should prevent the tail spikes without a full rollback.

sophia: Created issue #834: "seqlen-gated kernel hysteresis + kv_frag score" and drafted PR at github.com/redwood/ri/pull/4189. I'll post full traces and the flamegraph link here after sweep: http://perf.internal/reports/3023456789

deploy-bot: Canary status update: 3/5 hosts updated. Observed 2 hosts with increased 99.9p. Rolling back on those two hosts (ROLLBACK initiated).

jen: Thanks everyone. Quick sync tomorrow 10:00 to decide thresholds. @liam @amar please bring sweep results and a short proposal (hysteresis ms, kv_frag threshold, block size defaults).

liam: I'll sketch a proposal: thresholds [32,128,384], hysteresis=8 tokens (~5ms), kv_frag threshold=0.7, fallback kernel= paged-v1.

amar: I'll attach microbench CSV once done.

sophia: Uploaded flamegraph + traces to the perf link. Will follow up with PR comments on 4189.

jen: Awesome. Keep the thread updated and flag if rollback completes or stabilizes. :thumbsup:
